lines: אֵין הֶבְדֵּל בְּמָקוֹם אוֹ בִּזְמַן אֶצְלִי

review: 4:1–4:2 יֵהָפֵךְ הַכֶּלֶא … לְגַן / יָפְיוֹ יִשְׁבֶּה מִשֶּׁמֶשׁ וּמִיָּרֵחַ — the Arabic فَالسِّجْنُ يُمْسِي بِهِ رَوْضًا … تَسْبِي، وَتَزْرِي سَنًى بِالشَّمْسِ وَالْقَمَرِ is 'prison becomes with Him a garden; His beauties enchant and outshine sun and moon'; the Hebrew keeps both clauses, with שָׁבָה ('take captive') for the enchanting.

1:2 לַלֵּב … כָּל־חֶפְצוֹ — the Arabic لِلْقَلْبِ فِي ذَا الْمُحَيَّا غَايَةُ الْوَطَرِ is 'for the heart in that face is the utmost of desire'; חֵפֶץ is the biblical noun for what one delights in (Isa 58:13), and the line keeps the face as the object, not the means.

3:2 חַיֵּי שֶׁפַע וּפִרְיוֹן — the Arabic حَيَاةَ الْخِصْبِ وَالثَّمَرِ is 'a life of fertility and fruit'; שֶׁפַע is the biblical abundance (Deut 33:19) and פִּרְיוֹן its fruitfulness, so the pair stays agricultural rather than abstract.

5:1–5:2 אֵין הֶבְדֵּל בְּמָקוֹם אוֹ בִזְמַן … לַנִּצָּחוֹן — the Arabic لَا فَرْقَ فِي مَوْضِعٍ عِنْدِي وَلا زَمَنِ / مَا دَامَ فِيَّ يَقُودُ النَّفْسَ لِلظَّفَرِ keeps place and time in one line and the leading to triumph in the other; the Hebrew keeps both halves, with נִצָּחוֹן as the goal.
The print gives the hymn five two-line stanzas (5×2); the payload keeps that shape rather than pairing the stanzas into longer units.
